sunny.name: Sunny
sunny.science: High pressure brings sinking air, which keeps clouds from forming. Sunny days dry soil out fast, so check your crops' water.

cloudy.name: Cloudy
cloudy.science: Clouds form when rising air cools and its water vapor condenses into tiny droplets. Flat gray stratus clouds rarely bring heavy rain.

rain.name: Rain
rain.tv: Rain all day. Your outdoor crops will be watered for you!
rain.science: Rain falls when cloud droplets bump together and grow too heavy to float. Covered soil soaks rain in; bare soil can wash away.

storm.name: Thunderstorm
storm.tv: Thunderstorms! Heavy rain can wash bare soil away.
storm.science: Tall cumulonimbus clouds build when warm, moist air rises fast. Lightning even turns some nitrogen in the air into plant food that rain carries to the soil.

heat.name: Heat wave
heat.tv: Very hot and dry. Soil will dry out fast. Mulch helps!
heat.science: In a heat wave, water evaporates from soil and leaves much faster. Mulch shades the ground, and soil rich in organic matter holds more water.

fog.name: Foggy
fog.tv: Foggy and damp. A good day for mushrooms.
fog.science: Fog is a cloud touching the ground. It forms when moist air cools to its dew point. Damp, still days are when mushrooms pop up.

frost.name: Frost
frost.tv: Frost tonight! Tender crops outside could freeze.
frost.science: Frost forms on clear, calm nights when the ground loses heat to the sky and drops below freezing. Ice crystals inside plant cells can burst them.

snow.name: Snow
snow.tv: Snow is falling. Only the greenhouse can grow crops now.
snow.science: Snow forms when water vapor freezes straight into ice crystals high in cold clouds. A snow blanket actually insulates the soil below.
